key_functionalities: Registers the Surface integration kernel service as a demand-start driver and associates it with the ACPI device ID ACPI\MSHW0530.
Provides Windows 10 and Windows 11 power-policy packages and corresponding device properties for the operating system to use.
Sets PlatformKipSupported to enable the platform's KIP-related power-saving capability, as described in the INF comment.
Supplies 14 brightness-percent and backlight-power calibration points to Windows display energy estimation; sets the listed display-panel power estimation factors to zero.
Sets UserBatteryDischargeEstimator to 0xFFFFFFFF, with the INF comment indicating this hides estimated remaining battery discharge time.
Sets fvevol MaxEncryptRequests, MaxCryptoRequestsPerIo, and MaxDecryptRequests to 0x40; the INF comment identifies the encrypt request limit as an SSD-performance tuning setting under BitLocker.
extracted_details.major_components_functionalities_descrip: This package is SurfaceIntegrationDriver version 120.8.4.0, dated 05/06/2026 in the supplied INF, and the INFDescriptionData was semantically analyzed in detail. It binds the Surface integration kernel driver to ACPI\MSHW0530 and installs the service as demand-start. Its INF stages Windows 10 and Windows 11 power-policy packages and configures KIP support, battery-estimator visibility, long-press power-button screen refresh, and BitLocker request limits. It also provides a 14-point brightness-to-backlight-power curve and sets four display-panel estimation factors to zero. No official release notes for this exact version were available from the accessed sources, so the listed functionality reflects INF configuration rather than confirmed release changes.
impact_details: Power and energy estimation: the INF supplies brightness-dependent backlight power data and display-panel estimation settings, which may affect reported display energy use.
Platform power behavior: the INF enables the PlatformKipSupported setting; the INF comment says this enables KIP power-saving features.
Battery user interface: the INF comment states that the configured battery discharge estimator setting hides estimated time to discharge.
Power-button behavior: the INF enables the setting named EnableScreenRefreshOnPowerButtonLongPress; its exact user-visible effect beyond that named setting is not documented in the INF.

BitLocker and storage performance: the INF configures fvevol encryption, crypto-per-I/O, and decryption request limits to 0x40; the INF specifically associates the encrypt request limit with SSD performance under BitLocker.

Windows power-policy selection: the driver exposes policy packages for Windows 10 and Windows 11; actual selection and resulting policy behavior depend on the consuming operating-system/platform logic.
